solutions.latex:
Share of rent $= \dfrac{492}{4} \times 2 = \$246$

Total yearly utility bills $= 4 \times (572 + 260) = \$3328$

Sienna's share in bills $= (3328 \div 26) \div 4 = \$32$

Current accommodation expenses $= 246 + 32 = \$278$

20\% increase: $1.2 \times 278 = \$333.60$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct response; 2: makes progress towards current accommodation expenses; 1: finds share in utility bills

solutions.latex:
Fortnightly car loan payment $= 572 \times \dfrac{12}{26} = \$264$

Running costs $= 48 \times 2 = \$96$

Fortnightly bills $= 1831.70 \div 26 = \$70.45$

Total car budget $= 264 + 96 + 70.45 = \$430.45$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct answer; 1: at least 2 correct fortnightly amounts

solutions.latex:
Fortnightly food and groceries $= 145 \times 2 = \$290$

Fortnightly lunch and incidentals $= 40 \times 14 = \$560$

Total budget $= 333.60 + 430.45 + 290 + 560 = \$1614.05$ (consequential from parts (a) and (b))

Savings $= 1964 - 1614.05 = \$349.95$

solutions.latex:
At the break-even point $R = C$.

Substitute $n = 20$:

$C = 400 + 5(20) = 500$

$R = 25 \times 20 = 500$

Since both equations have the same value, the company breaks even when 20 items were delivered.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: shows correct break-even; 1: substitutes $n = 20$ into either equation

solutions.latex:
$P = R - C = 25n - (5n + 400) = 25n - 5n - 400 = 20n - 400$

If $P = 600$, then $600 = 20n - 400$, so $1000 = 20n$ and $n = 50$.

Therefore 50 orders were produced and delivered.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct answer; 1: works toward profit equation $P = 20n - 400$ (stating $P = 600$ is not enough for a mark)
